comparator.sourceNotes: Current allocation is reconstructed as first year60 + fixed upper-year35 + four alternating-cycle units30 + three concrete seminars15 + thesis10 + genuine open30 =180 EC. The selected legal-French practical seminar and two research seminars meet the current three-seminar/two-research rule. Alternants are counted once across the two-year cycle; Poetry and Theatre10 and Metamorphoses of the Novel5 are explicitly not offered in 2026–2027, so this is a degree allocation rather than a claim that all units run in one year. The adopted formal rules state no specialisation and Dutch/French instruction.

alternatives.label: Colonial histories, global literature & cultural power
alternatives.concept: Study literature, empire, colonial and postcolonial histories, cultural institutions, media and language/power across global contexts. Treat these as related humanities and social-science approaches while preserving the absence of French-language proficiency and a French-specific literary sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The label names the completed curriculum’s actual literature, empire, media, heritage and power content without claiming French-language study or a full Francophone-area curriculum.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and ten level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; the only formal prerequisite, Introduction to Brain & Behavior for Psycholinguistics, occurs two semesters earlier. Introductory literary, historical, sociological and film study precedes advanced interpretation, media, heritage and research seminars. No additional French-language prerequisite or proficiency is invented.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & language in cultural expression
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic and media forms create meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal cultural production.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film and media; it is labelled as cultural-expression study and not as French proficiency or French linguistics.
progression: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and eight level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Introductory literature, rhetoric, sociology and film/media precede advanced stylistic, persuasive, creative, interpretive and documentary work. No French-language competence is implied by this progression.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. History Research Seminar, European Union Politics and three art/heritage courses are replaced by Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action, Persuasive Communication, Creative Communication Laboratory and From T.V. to TikTok. The change moves advanced study from colonial history, heritage and cultural institutions to language, rhetoric and mediated expression.

Advanced French proficiency and French linguistics

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. A third French-language proficiency and linguistics programme is not feasible: the workbook contains no French-language sequence, advanced French grammar/phonetics/composition, translation or French-specific linguistic research. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as French proficiency.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study global literature, colonial and postcolonial history, cultural institutions, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and language/power. UCR does not offer the required French proficiency progression, French grammar and phonetics, translation, or cumulative French and Francophone literature seminars, so these are related humanities routes rather than full French Language and Culture equivalents.
